867-mrs-korner-sins-her-mercies.creator: Jerome K. Jerome
867-mrs-korner-sins-her-mercies.description: A book by Jerome K. Jerome. “Perhaps,” suggested the kindly bosom friend, ever the one to plead the cause of the transgressor, “perhaps he was swearing, and she did not hear him. You see, if he had his head well underneath the bed--”

arxiv-1806-03537.title: Diachronic word embeddings and semantic shifts: a survey
arxiv-1806-03537.creator: Andrey Kutuzov Lilja Øvrelid Terrence Szymanski Erik Velldal[0.5ex] University of Oslo, Norway {andreku | liljao | erikve}@ifi.uio.no, [0.5ex] ANZ, Melbourne, Australia terry.szymanski@gmail.com
arxiv-1806-03537.description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed a surge of publications aimed at tracing temporal changes in lexical semantics using distributional methods, particularly prediction-based word embedding models. However, this vein of research lacks the cohesion, common terminology and shared practices of more established areas of natural language processing.

arxiv-2102-01445.title: Prediction of low-keV monochromatic images from polyenergetic CT scans for improved automatic detection of pulmonary embolism
arxiv-2102-01445.creator: Constantin Seibold ∗1 , Matthias A. Fink ∗2 ,Charlotte Goos 1 , Hans-Ulrich Kauczor 2 Heinz-Peter Schlemmer 3 \textit{Heinz-Peter Schlemmer}^{3} , Rainer Stiefelhagen 1 , Jens Kleesiek 3,4
arxiv-2102-01445.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Constantin Seibold ∗1 , Matthias A. Fink ∗2 ,Charlotte Goos 1 , Hans-Ulrich Kauczor 2 Heinz-Peter Schlemmer 3 \textit{Heinz-Peter Schlemmer}^{3} , Rainer Stiefelhagen 1 , Jens Kleesiek 3,4. Detector-based spectral computed tomography is a recent dual-energy CT (DECT) technology that offers the possibility of obtaining spectral information. From this spectral data, different types of images can be derived, amongst others virtual monoenergetic ( monoE ) images.

arxiv-2303-04166.title: Deterministic Storage and Retrieval of Telecom Quantum Dot Photons Interfaced with an Atomic Quantum Memory
arxiv-2303-04166.creator: S. E. Thomas 1 † , L. Wagner 2 † , R. Joos 2 , R. Sittig 2 , C. Nawrath 2 , P. Burdekin 1 , T. Huber-Loyola 3 , S. Sagona-Stophel 1 , S. Höfling 3 , M. Jetter 2 , P. Michler 2 , I. A. Walmsley 1 , S. L. Portalupi 2 , P. M. Ledingham 4
arxiv-2303-04166.description: Abstract A hybrid interface of solid state single-photon sources and atomic quantum memories is a long sought-after goal in photonic quantum technologies. Here we demonstrate deterministic storage and retrieval of photons from a semiconductor quantum dot in an atomic ensemble quantum memory at telecommunications wavelengths.

arxiv-2411-17964.title: Probing topological degeneracy on a torus using superconducting altermagnets
arxiv-2411-17964.creator: Tsz Fung Heung, Marcel Franz
arxiv-2411-17964.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tsz Fung Heung, Marcel Franz. The notion of topological order (TO) can be defined through the characteristic ground state degeneracy of a system placed on a manifold with non-zero genus g g , such as a torus. This ground state degeneracy has served as a key tool for identifying TOs in theoretical calculations but it has never been possible to probe experimentally because fabricating a device in the requisite toroidal geometry is generally not feasible.

arxiv-2412-19046.title: Thermal quantum correlations of a single electron in a double quantum dot with transverse magnetic field
arxiv-2412-19046.creator: Vinicius Leitão 1 , Onofre Rojas 1 , Moises Rojas 1
arxiv-2412-19046.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the thermal quantum correlations in a semiconductor double quantum dot system. The device comprises a single electron in a double quantum dot subjected to a longitudinal magnetic field and a transverse magnetic field gradient. The thermal entanglement of the single electron is driven by the charge and spin qubits.

arxiv-2504-18342.title: Probing Quantum Phenomena through Photoproduction in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2504-18342.creator: James Daniel Brandenburg, Spencer R. Klein, Zhangbu Xu, Shuai Yang, Wangmei Zha, Jian Zhou
arxiv-2504-18342.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by James Daniel Brandenburg, Spencer R. Klein, Zhangbu Xu, Shuai Yang, Wangmei Zha, Jian Zhou. Photoproduction in ultra-peripheral relativistic heavy-ion collisions displays many unique features, often involving quantum mechanical coherence and two-source interference between photon emission from the two ions. We review the recent experimental results from RHIC and the LHC and theoretical studies of coherent vector meson photoproduction, emphasizing the quantum mechanical aspects of the interactions and the entanglement between the final state particles.

arxiv-2504-19734.title: LLM-Assisted Automated Deductive Coding of Dialogue Data: Leveraging Dialogue-Specific Characteristics to Enhance Contextual Understanding
arxiv-2504-19734.creator: Ying Na, Shihui Feng
arxiv-2504-19734.description: Abstract Dialogue data has been a key source for understanding learning processes, offering critical insights into how students engage in collaborative discussions and how these interactions shape their knowledge construction. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has introduced promising opportunities for advancing qualitative research, particularly in the automated coding of dialogue data.

arxiv-2506-05764.title: Exploring Microstructural Dynamics in Cryptocurrency Limit Order Books: Better Inputs Matter More Than Stacking Another Hidden Layer
arxiv-2506-05764.creator: Haochuan (Kevin) Wang
arxiv-2506-05764.description: Abstract Cryptocurrency price dynamics are driven largely by microstructural supply–demand imbalances in the limit order book (LOB), yet the highly noisy nature of LOB data complicates the signal extraction process. Prior research has demonstrated that deep‐learning architectures can yield promising predictive performance on pre‐processed equity and futures LOB data, but they often treat model complexity as an unqualified virtue.

arxiv-2509-12345.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to asymptotic analysis of Toeplitz+Hankel determinants II
arxiv-2509-12345.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . In this article, we continue the development of the Riemann–Hilbert formalism for studying the asymptotics of Toeplitz+Hankel determinants with non-identical symbols, which we initiated in [ 26 ] . In [ 26 ] , we showed that the Riemann–Hilbert problem we formulated admits the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis, but with a special restriction on the winding numbers of the associated symbols. In particular, the most natural case, namely zero winding numbers, is not allowed.

arxiv-2602-14145.title: Kinematic Evidence for Open Cluster Origins of Galactic Binary Neutron Stars astropy ( 6 ; 4 ; 5 ) , Galpy ( 12 ) , Matplotlib ( 26 ) , Numpy ( 22 ) .
arxiv-2602-14145.creator: Wen-Jie Yu, Lu Zhou, Zhi-Qiang You, Hao Ding, Lu Li, Long Wang, Xing-Jiang Zhu
arxiv-2602-14145.description: Abstract We investigate the potential birthplace of Galactic binary neutron star (BNS) systems through a kinematic analysis. Using high-precision astrometry from Gaia DR3, updated pulsar distances, and Monte Carlo sampling of astrometric errors, we integrate the past trajectories of 11 Galactic BNSs and 167 globular clusters plus 2967 open clusters, to search for past encounters.

pmc-11506225.description: The regulation of energy in the brain has garnered substantial attention in recent years due to its significant implications in various disorders and aging. pmc-12749261.title: Integrating small mammal personality and population abundance into forest regeneration predictions for a managed, mixed species forest in Maine, USA

pmc-12749261.description: Understanding forest regeneration is critical for predicting the future of forests, but most forest growth models overlook the animals responsible for driving regeneration dynamics. Scatter-hoarding small mammals are critical for the regeneration of many keystone plant species, and their personality influences their role in the seed dispersal process.

pmc-12960972.title: Changes in levels of endocannabinoidome mediators in mice with cancer cachexia: links with steatosis and gut microbial dysbiosis
pmc-12960972.creator: Alexandra L. Degraeve, Adele Cutignano, Fabiana Piscitelli, Rosaria Villano, Giulia De Simone, Roberta Verde, Morgane M. Thibaut, Laure B. Bindels, Vincenzo Di Marzo
pmc-12960972.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCachexia is a debilitating syndrome associated with involuntary weight loss, often occurring in cancer patients. In both humans and animal models, alterations in endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling occur in association with both metabolic disorders and several types of tumors. The wider signaling system, including the two eCBs, anandamide (AEA) and 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol (2-AG), their congeners and other long chain fatty acid amides, as well as their metabolic enzymes and receptors, is known as endocannabinoidome (eCBome).

pmc-13551469.title: Artificial intelligence in infection prevention and control education: toward intelligent, real-time clinical learning systems
pmc-13551469.creator: Yu-long Cao, Na Liu, Fang Wang, Jiao Shan, Xiao-yuan Bao, Meng Jin, Wei Huai, Yi-cheng Jin, Yi-xi Jin, Zhi-ning Zhang, Ji-qiu Kuang
pmc-13551469.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in infection prevention and control (IPC) education as a means of addressing limitations of conventional training, including limited scalability, delayed feedback, and subjective competency assessment. This mini review summarizes emerging applications of AI-enabled technologies in IPC education and examines their potential educational benefits, limitations, and implementation considerations.

pmc-13572637.creator: Hong-mei Chen, Li-nong Wang, Yan-bing Fu, Jun Hua
pmc-13572637.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo develop and internally validate an explainable machine learning model for early mortality prediction in pediatric sepsis using routinely available clinical variables, to support clinical risk stratification and decision-making.MethodsA total of 752 children with sepsis admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between January 1, 2019, and June 30, 2023, were retrospectively enrolled. Twenty-six routinely available clinical variables obtained within 24 h after PICU admission were included.
